subject: Pharmacology & Dental Materials
title: Separate drug handling from material structure
summary: Learn pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics and the composition of two restorative material families.

units.title: Follow what the body does to a drug
units.lesson: Pharmacokinetics describes drug concentrations over time. Absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination organize the main processes. These explain why administration and the concentration at a site are not identical events. Understanding the processes does not authorize a dose change; this chapter contains no prescribing instructions.
units.question: Which list describes pharmacokinetic processes?
units.explanation: ADME organizes how the body handles a drug.

units.title: Follow what a drug does to the body
units.lesson: Pharmacodynamics describes drug effects and mechanisms, including interactions with receptors and relationships between concentration or dose and response. Keep it distinct from absorption or elimination. A theory item about receptor-mediated effect is asking a different question from a concentration-time curve. No drug, dose or treatment choice is recommended here.
units.question: Which topic is pharmacodynamic?
choices: The colour of a tablet box
units.explanation: Pharmacodynamics concerns how a drug produces an effect.
rationales: Packaging colour is not the mechanism.

units.title: Recognize a composite structure
units.lesson: Resin-based dental composite combines a resin matrix with inorganic filler and a coupling system. The name describes a combination of phases, not a single pure metal. Components contribute different properties. This academic composition lesson does not select a material for a patient or establish comparative clinical longevity.
units.question: Which description fits resin-based dental composite?
units.explanation: Resin composites combine matrix and filler phases.
rationales: Water alone is not a composite.

units.title: Recognize conventional glass ionomer
units.lesson: Conventional glass ionomer is based on an acid–base reaction involving ion-leachable glass and a polyacid component. Resin-modified glass ionomer adds resin chemistry, so the names should not be treated as identical formulations. Composition describes material families; handling, indications and patient-specific selection require additional information.
units.question: Which chemistry is central to conventional glass ionomer?
choices: An acid–base reaction involving glass and polyacid
units.explanation: Glass ionomer chemistry involves an acid–base reaction.
rationales: Evaporation alone does not describe it.

units.question: A viva asks how receptor interaction produces a drug’s effect. Which branch addresses it most directly?
units.explanation: Mechanism and effect belong to pharmacodynamics.

units.question: A materials question lists resin matrix, inorganic filler and coupling system. Which family is identified?
